title: piacere: mi piace, mi piacciono
rule: The thing liked is the subject; the person is an indirect object: mi (to me), ti (to you), gli / le (to him / her), ci, vi, gli (to them). Piace with a singular or an infinitive, piacciono with a plural.

head: Person
+ singular / infinitive
+ plural
English
rows: mi piace il caffè · mi piace ballare
blocks.note: Units 3 and 7 use mi and ti; the full table is for reference now and for unit 7.

blocks.text: With a name or a stressed pronoun

items.t: A Dora piace il caffè amaro.
items.n: Dora likes her coffee without sugar.

items.t: A me piace il cappuccino, a lui piace il caffè.
items.n: I like cappuccino, he likes coffee.
items.note: a me, a te, a lui, a lei for emphasis and contrast

items.t: A chi piace il tè? — A nessuno.
Anche a me. / Neanche a me.
items.note: not anche io: the liker is a me

head: Verb
Example
English
rows: Mi manca Toronto. Mi mancano i miei.
I miss Toronto. I miss my family.
Mi serve una chiave. Mi servono due tazzine.
I need a key. I need two cups.
A coffee is enough for me.
blocks.note: All built the same way; unit 13 practises them.

blocks.title: Piacere is also a verb like the others
blocks.text: [[Io piaccio a Dora]] = Dora likes me (I am pleasing to Dora). [[Piaci a tutti]] = everyone likes you. Useful, but rarer than mi piace. The full conjugation is on the Verbs page.

items.wrong: Anche io! (answering mi piace il caffè)
items.why: The liker is an indirect object: a me.
Infinitives are singular, even two of them.
The person needs a (or gli / le).

items.q: A Pasquale ___ il caffè amaro; a Dora ___ i cornetti alla crema.
items.n: Pasquale likes black coffee; Dora likes cream croissants.

items.why: Me too, with piacere: anche a me.
